title: Veritasium: Publications (lists Muller, Bewes, Sharma & Reimann 2008, 'Saying the wrong thing: improving learning with multimedia by including misconceptions', J. Computer Assisted Learning 24(2):144-155, and Muller's 2008 Sydney PhD)
what_it_supports: Citation and existence of the 2008 JCAL paper and the PhD thesis. The d~0.79/0.83 refutation-vs-concise effect sizes and the 'low prior knowledge benefited most' result come from a search-tool summary of the abstract (DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2729.2007.00248.x); full text not opened.

title: Muller & Sharma: Tackling misconceptions in introductory physics using multimedia presentations (Univ. Sydney open journals; Proc. Australian Conf. on Science and Mathematics Education)
what_it_supports: Abstract: misconceptions give a false sense of knowing (less effort) and interfere with memory of new concepts; exposing students to common misconceptions, even non-interactively, can help. No effect sizes on the page.

title: Scientific American: How YouTube star Derek Muller of Veritasium is challenging scientific... (28 May 2025)
what_it_supports: Muller's stated approach: confusion/friction helps learning; his PhD compared a polished textbook-style video (easier to follow, little learning) with one showing a student struggling (more improvement); Veritasium poses questions and asks viewers to predict before the reveal; began as short street-quiz clips. Fetched summary of the article.

title: Tubefilter: Veritasium signs with A3 Artists Agency (8 Sep 2022)
what_it_supports: Veritasium launched 2011 drawing on Muller's physics-education PhD; became known for videos asking the public science questions that exposed misconceptions.

title: Crouch, Fagen, Callan & Mazur (2004) Classroom demonstrations: learning tools or entertainment? Am. J. Phys. 72:835-838 (Compadre record)
what_it_supports: Students who only watched a demonstration understood the concepts no better than students who never saw it; predicting the outcome first gave significantly greater understanding. Effect sizes 0.09/0.36/0.45 appear only in a secondary blog (unverified).

title: Szpunar, Khan & Schacter (2013) Interpolated memory tests reduce mind wandering and improve learning of online lectures, PNAS 110(16):6313-6317 (PMC record)
what_it_supports: Tests interleaved into online lectures reduced mind-wandering (baseline about 40%), increased note-taking and improved later learning. Seen via search-tool summary of abstract/interview; page not opened by me.

title: Richland, Kornell & Kao (2009) The pretesting effect: do unsuccessful retrieval attempts enhance learning? J. Exp. Psychology: Applied 15(3)
what_it_supports: Pre-questions help later learning even when the initial answer is wrong, provided corrective feedback follows; the paper notes unretrieved items show little benefit without feedback. Search-tool summary; PDF not opened by me.

title: Faculty Focus: Student learning in 3 seconds (secondary summary of Rowe's wait-time research)
what_it_supports: Classroom wait-time lore of about 3 s (Rowe); secondary, older and soft evidence; no video-specific data. Used only to show a 5 s silent window is not supported and 1.4 s is below classroom guidance.

title: Wikipedia: Hypercorrection (psychology) (secondary; original Butterfield & Metcalfe 2001, J. Exp. Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition 27(6):1491-1494)
what_it_supports: High-confidence errors are more likely to be corrected on retest than low-confidence errors; attention to feedback rises after confident errors. Original paper not opened.

title: Chen & Klahr (1999) All other things being equal: acquisition and transfer of the control of variables strategy, Child Development 70(5):1098-1120 (CMU PDF)
what_it_supports: Explicit training plus probe questions taught 7-10-year-olds to control variables and transfer it; the 40% to 80% figure is from Klahr & Nigam's later summary as relayed by a search tool; PDF not opened.

title: Li & Singh: Students' difficulties with equations involving circuit elements (arXiv:1602.04872; PERC 2012 proceedings)
what_it_supports: Abstract: introductory students struggle to see how an ohmic resistor's resistance, written as V/I, does not change when V is varied. Abstract only.

title: Schwartz & Bransford (1998) A time for telling, Cognition and Instruction 16(4):475-522 (PDF)
what_it_supports: Students who analysed contrasting cases (inventing graphs) before a lecture learned and transferred more than those who first summarised a text; explicit telling works best after preparation. Search-tool summary of abstract; PDF not opened.

title: The expertise reversal effect (Educational Psychologist 38(1):23-31, 2003; Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler & Sweller) (UOW record)
what_it_supports: Techniques that help novices (worked examples, integrated text) can lose effect or backfire for more experienced learners; basis for guiding weak-foundation learners. Abstract-level.

title: Renkl & Atkinson (2003) Structuring the transition from example study to problem solving in cognitive skill acquisition: a cognitive load perspective, Educational Psychologist 38:15-22 (record)
what_it_supports: Worked examples are most effective in early skill acquisition, problem solving later; fade solution steps gradually (backward fading) as intrinsic load falls. Abstract-level.

title: Heer & Robertson (2007) Animated transitions in statistical data graphics, IEEE InfoVis (PDF)
what_it_supports: Two controlled experiments: animated transitions improved graphical perception (object tracking, value estimation) over static transitions; guidelines follow Tversky et al.'s congruence and apprehension. Abstract/summary level; caveats about timing and axis re-scaling relayed second-hand.

title: Ozcelik, Karakus, Kursun & Cagiltay (2009) An eye-tracking study of how color coding affects multimedia learning, Computers & Education 53(2):445-453
what_it_supports: N=52; colour-coded materials improved retention and transfer; learners found matching text/illustration information more efficiently. Abstract-level.

title: Alpizar, Adesope & Wong (2020) A meta-analysis of signaling principle in multimedia learning environments, ETR&D 68:2095-2119
what_it_supports: 44 effect sizes from 29 experiments (N=2,726); overall d=.38. Abstract-level.

title: Cambridge Handbook of Multimedia Learning (3rd ed.): Principles for reducing extraneous processing (coherence, signaling, redundancy, spatial and temporal contiguity)
what_it_supports: Coherence: support in 23 of 23 tests, median d=0.86; signaling: 24 of 28 tests, median d=0.41 (3rd-edition figures as relayed by search tool; the 2nd edition gives different values, e.g. coherence 1.32). Page seen only as a search result.

title: The Learning Scientists: Designing effective instructional videos (summary of Mayer 2021, JARMAC)
what_it_supports: Mayer lists 14 video principles; this summary covers multimedia, signaling (flag key material), segmenting and personalization. The JARMAC abstract (seen via search summary, not opened) lists pre-training among the principles.

title: Rey et al. (2019) A meta-analysis of the segmenting effect, Educational Psychology Review 31:389-419
what_it_supports: 56 studies, 88 comparisons: small-to-medium benefit for retention and transfer, lower cognitive load, longer learning time. Abstract-level via search summary.

title: WSU News: Seductive details inhibit learning (Sundararajan & Adesope, Educational Psychology Review, 2020)
what_it_supports: Meta-analysis of 58 studies (>7,500 students): interesting-but-irrelevant details (jokes, cat videos, background music) lowered learning; harm larger beside relevant diagrams and for static details; most studies 6-12 minutes. The g=-0.33 figure is only in a secondary summary.

title: Moreno & Mayer (2000) A coherence effect in multimedia learning: the case for minimizing irrelevant sounds, J. Educational Psychology 92(1):117-125 (PDF is a scan)
what_it_supports: Adding background music and/or environmental sounds to narrated animations lowered retention and transfer (sound-only effect in Exp. 2). Abstract-level via search summary; scanned PDF not machine-readable.

title: Kampfe, Sedlmeier & Renkewitz (2011) The impact of background music on adult listeners: a meta-analysis, Psychology of Music 39(4):424-448
what_it_supports: Overall null effect; music interferes with reading, small detrimental effect on memory, positive effects on emotion and sports performance; few studies allowed effect sizes. Abstract-level.

title: Impact of background music on reading comprehension: influence of lyrics language and study habits, Frontiers in Psychology (2024)
what_it_supports: Vocal music reduced reading comprehension versus no music, most when lyrics were in the same language as the text; habitual music listeners less affected. Search-summary level.

title: Guo, Kim & Rubin (2014) How video production affects student engagement: an empirical study of MOOC videos, ACM Learning at Scale (PDF)
what_it_supports: Read in full via pdftotext: 6.9M edX sessions; videos under 6 minutes engage most; Khan-style tablet drawing held viewers 1.5-2x as long as slides/code and 40% vs 31% went on to attempt problems; best tutorials had planned layout; faster speaking (mean 156 wpm, range 48-254) engaged more, with the 145-165 wpm bucket least energetic. MOOC context; engagement time, not learning.

title: Gentner & Gentner (1983) Flowing waters or teeming crowds: mental models of electricity, in Mental Models (PDF)
what_it_supports: Read in full via pdftotext: different analogies produce systematically different inferences; the flowing-fluid model helped with batteries, the moving-crowd (gates) model with resistors; a subject using the pipe model wrongly predicted less current for parallel resistors and corrected it with the crowd model.

title: Common misunderstandings of electricity: analysis of interview responses of electrical engineering technology students (iJEP)
what_it_supports: Students kept applying an incorrect water-analogy to current and treated electricity as a substance that can be used up. Abstract via search summary.

title: Yarroch (1985) Student understanding of chemical equation balancing, J. Research in Science Teaching 22(5):449-459 (MTU record)
what_it_supports: Students with weak grasp of subscripts were willing to break the rule against changing them when balancing; those with consistent particle diagrams grasped subscripts. Record-level.

title: Kang et al. (2009) The wick in the candle of learning: epistemic curiosity activates reward circuitry and enhances memory, Psychological Science 20(8):963-973 (CMU PDF)
what_it_supports: Read in full via pdftotext: curiosity is an inverted-U function of confidence; higher curiosity predicted better recall of surprising answers 1-2 weeks later; frames curiosity as an information gap (Loewenstein 1994).

title: Faculty Focus: Humor in the classroom, 40 years of research (summary of Banas, Dunbar, Rodriguez & Liu 2011, Communication Education 60(1):115-144)
what_it_supports: Content-related, non-hostile humour is appropriate; mocking or disparaging humour is harmful; humour reliably aids attention and interest while evidence on learning is mixed; laugh with students, not at them. Secondary summary; original not opened.

title: Teaching and learning with instructional humor: a review of five-decades research and further direction, Frontiers in Psychology (2025)
what_it_supports: Narrative review of about 140 works: related humour most consistently beneficial; unrelated humour mixed; self-disparaging humour neutral for learning but warming; aggressive humour generally worse; optimal frequency for online/video unclear. First 100k characters read.

title: APLU/NTED: Humor to engage students (secondary citing Kaplan & Pascoe 1977, J. Educational Psychology 69:61-65)
what_it_supports: Concept-related humorous examples improved retention on delayed tests (6 weeks) though not immediate comprehension. Secondary; original not opened.

title: Lab News: Q&A with Steve Mould (23 Oct 2018)
what_it_supports: Mould says the ah-ha moment of understanding matters more than the ha-ha of entertainment. Nothing on his topic choice or demonstration method on this page.

title: The Stanford Daily: 3Blue1Brown creator Grant Sanderson '15 talks engaging with math using stories and visuals (24 Jan 2020)
what_it_supports: Sanderson starts with visuals and then articulates meaning, which gives learners ownership; treats explanation like story; emphasises emotion, wonder and imagination over usefulness.

title: 3Blue1Brown: FAQ
what_it_supports: Sentences confirmed verbatim on a second fetch: every movement should be deliberate with an identifiable purpose; definitions are an ending point, not a starting point; best pedagogical order often differs from logical order; each visual and movement should make the same point as the narration. Undated page.

title: Kurzgesagt: Our video process
what_it_supports: Stages: research with sourcesheet and expert check; script that 'can take about a dozen drafts'; sketching of visual metaphors then illustration; narrator's voice-over sets timing for animators; specially composed soundtrack per video. No dates or hour counts on the page.

title: Education Week: Professor Dave Explains, how he attracted 345,000 YouTube subscribers (Mar 2019)
what_it_supports: Farina positions his videos between hook-driven edutainment and long Khan-style lectures, aiming for depth after the hook; audience is high-school and undergraduate students; he does writing, filming, editing and animation himself.

title: Tubefilter: YouTube Millionaires, Professor Dave (28 Jul 2022)
what_it_supports: Removes filler and gives viewers only what they need ('guided learning'), highlights keywords, uses diagrams and directs attention to the right place at the right time; breaks complex subjects into digestible parts; no longer appears on camera; uses writers; Premiere and After Effects.

title: The Falconer (Torrey Pines High School): Q&A with Professor Dave Explains (7 Nov 2024)
what_it_supports: A writer drafts the script; Farina edits lightly, narrates, then plans visuals (improvised in After Effects); academic and precise, avoids songs and characters; anticipates common pitfalls from classroom experience; treats comprehension as the engagement measure.

title: Digiday: The secret sauce behind YouTube giant Vsauce (4 Dec 2014)
what_it_supports: Stevens writes down facts that surprise him and connects them into a script; follows questions down the rabbit hole; long descriptions act as bibliographies; researches and writes alone.

title: Unsung (Marcin Wichary): Three good interactive explainers (2 Jun 2026)
what_it_supports: Ciechanowski's 'Curves and Surfaces' colour-matches key ideas between text and interactive elements and offers undo.

title: Bartosz Ciechanowski: Lights and Shadows
what_it_supports: Builds from one source outward; most demos let the reader change one property per slider; text refers to diagram colours; states approximations (e.g. the inverse-square law holds accurately only for infinitely small light sources). No interview with him was found.

title: Wikipedia: MinutePhysics
what_it_supports: Whiteboard-animation style; early videos about one minute. Drawing-while-speaking and time-lapse come from a Live Science search summary (https://livescience.com/55121-youtube-channel-minute-physics.html, page body unreadable); scripting/recording process not found.

title: Cristobal et al. (2026) PaperTok: exploring the use of generative AI for creating short-form videos for research communication (arXiv:2601.18218, HTML), formative study N=8
what_it_supports: Creators/science communicators: hooks that correct a misconception, subvert an expectation or lead with an unexpected statistic; fast body with dynamic simple visuals; recommended 15-30 s (under 60 s at most); ending circles back to the opening promise and says what to do next; text overlays useful because feeds autoplay muted; robotic/AI-sounding narration caused disengagement; avoid long intros. Small qualitative study on research communication. First 100k characters read.

title: Educational short videos: bibliometric trends, thematic structure and operationalisation (arXiv:2608.06932, Aug 2026)
what_it_supports: 2,169 records; no consistent numerical threshold for 'short'; shortness should be judged by purpose and unit, not duration alone. Abstract-level.

title: Outlook India: interview with Alakh Pandey (3 Nov 2022, updated 18 Jan 2024)
what_it_supports: Because online students cannot ask, he tries to address even the smallest doubts; advises teachers to win the hearts of children; says teachers should not chase cheap fame by going viral. No statement about language or humour.

title: CBSE: Science (086) Marking Scheme, Class X, 2025-26 sample paper
what_it_supports: Read via pdftotext: model answers for numericals use 'Given data', Step 1 to Step 3 and a conclusion; e.g. I = V/R = 6/24 = 0.25 A. Mark splits within steps could not be extracted (formulas are images); stepwise-marking claims elsewhere are secondary.

title: Vedantu: CBSE Class 10 science practical (secondary)
what_it_supports: Class 10 practical list includes determining the dependence of potential difference across a resistor on current with a graph; FAQ refers to the 2026-27 session.

title: Bhatia (2020) Teaching code-mixed English (Hinglish) in India, FORTELL issue 40
what_it_supports: Conceptual paper with no classroom comprehension data; used only to show no controlled Hinglish-versus-English evidence was found. Search-summary level.

title: Assam State Board (SEBA/AHSEC) complete guide (secondary)
what_it_supports: Reports SEBA/AHSEC instruction and examination in Assamese, English, Bengali, Hindi, Bodo and Manipuri. Secondary; page not opened.

title: Wikipedia: 6-7 meme
what_it_supports: Popular from mid-2025 on TikTok and Reels; Dictionary.com 2025 Word of the Year (Oct 2025); school bans; by March 2026 teens still using it were mocked (Yahoo Life cited on the page).

title: Khaleej Times: Explained, from meme to movement, how 'Cockroach Party' inspired Indian students' protest (7 Jun 2026)
what_it_supports: Cockroach Janta Party: satirical youth collective launched May 2026 as a parody of the ruling party; protests over alleged exam irregularities; millions of followers.

title: Boston University College of Communication: profile of Cockroach Janta Party founder (8 Jun 2026)
what_it_supports: Founder Abhijeet Dipke; about 50,000 sign-ups in 24 hours, over one million in five days; Instagram account above 22 million followers; exam mismanagement among the concerns listed.

title: Storyboard18: Delhi HC backs Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, rules personality rights breach erodes celebrity dignity (11 Sep 2025)
what_it_supports: Interim protection granted 9 Sep 2025 (Justice Tejas Karia) against misuse of name and likeness via AI/deepfakes; takedowns within 72 hours. The article does not address memes or fan content.

title: Netflix Partner Help: English Timed Text Style Guide
what_it_supports: 42 characters per line, maximum two lines, up to 20 characters per second for adult programs and 17 for children's programs.

title: Reap: YouTube Shorts, Reels and TikTok safe zones (secondary)
what_it_supports: Third-party margins 288 top, 672 bottom, 48 left, 192 right at 1080x1920; ad-derived and not an official organic-Shorts spec; sources conflict. Seen via search summary.

title: Abrams & Christ (2003) Motion onset captures attention, Psychological Science 14(5):427-432 (PubMed)
what_it_supports: Attention is captured by the onset of motion rather than by motion itself. Abstract-level.

title: We Are Listen: What is sonic branding, part 2
what_it_supports: Practitioner view: audio logos about 2-3 s, textural ones 1-2 s, melodic ones built on 3-5 notes; cites no research.

title: Our Opus pilot builds: narration/timeline.json for physics, chemistry and biology (my calculation)
what_it_supports: My calc: first word 0.68-0.76 s; silent think gap 5.08-5.43 s; spoken disclosure beat 3.92-4.08 s at 74-77 wpm; non-teaching time 9.68-10.22 s = 14.0-14.4% of 67.1-73.2 s; teaching-beat pace 127-204 wpm per beat and 138-149 wpm overall excluding the think gap. Chemistry and biology files are siblings of the physics path.

title: Digest colour tokens (00_INPUTS_digest.md section 2) with my WCAG and colour-vision-deficiency calculation
what_it_supports: My calc: contrast vs paper #F5F2EA: voltage 5.98, current 4.52, resistance 5.76, error 6.08, muted 5.66; L* 39.0/46.7/40.1 for V/I/R; CIEDE2000 under simulated deuteranopia (Machado 2009 matrices, severity 1): resistance-error 10.0, current-muted 5.1. The phone type-size arithmetic (71 mm width, 35 cm assumed, ISO 9241 angles second-hand) is also mine.

title: GWU Teaching: TED-Ed (secondary)
what_it_supports: TED-Ed lesson shell is Watch, Think, Dig deeper, Discuss; no narrative-craft guidance found, so TED-Ed is listed as unverified.

title: Fostering learning from instructional video in a second language (Applied Cognitive Psychology, 2018)
what_it_supports: Korean university students: video plus narration plus text beat video plus narration, contradicting the redundancy principle for second-language learners. Summary-level.

title: Social Samosa: 91% of India's Next Gen pay more attention to brands that use humour (Snapchat and Omnicom study, 18 Sep 2026)
what_it_supports: 6,000+ users aged 13-28 in US, UK, Canada, France, Germany and India (India sample size not stated); 87% say humour is how their generation discusses serious things; about 80% say brands online feel like older people trying to joke; 79% say explaining a joke ruins it; self-deprecation and logic-underneath-randomness land; forced or out-of-touch humour is poorly received. Industry-commissioned, Snapchat-heavy; scope of the 80% figure unclear.

title: SME Street: PhysicsWallah's Alakh Pandey to expand presence across five South Indian states (24 Sep 2026)
what_it_supports: PW was originally known for Hinglish batches and now offers courses in Hindi, English, Hinglish and nine regional languages.

title: Google Ads Help: About video ad specs
what_it_supports: Safe-zone guidance for 1080x1920 vertical ads is an image template; pixel numbers are not in the page text and the page does not tie the zone to Shorts.

title: edu-physics.com: Experiment, Studying Ohm's Law with V-I Graph (4 Jun 2025)
what_it_supports: Rheostat varies current; ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel; slope of the V-I graph gives R; precaution: avoid high current because heating raises resistance; take readings quickly and switch off between them.
